raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On CUDA with a BF16 KV cache, `tilelang_sparse_fwd` always used the single-pass kernel, which launches one CTA per (token, 64-head block). Decode, MTP verify and draft batches are only a few tokens, so the kernel ran on 1-6 of 132 SMs. On GLM-5.3-Flash H200 TP8 that is ~100 us per call, about 10% of TPOT at C=1. The existing split-topk partial/combine kernels were only used on HIP and for FP8 KV.

## Modifications

- On SM90 with BF16 KV, calls with `tokens * padded_heads <= 1024` take the split-topk partial/combine path with one KV tile per CTA. Larger calls keep the single-pass kernel.
- Tests cover the gate at the 64/128-head cutoffs, which kernel runs on each side of the 8-head cutoff (checked against torch and CUDA graph replay), and keep the existing BF16 cases on the single-pass kernels.

Kernel sweep, H200, cold L2 (`marker.do_bench`). Each cell is split / single-pass (us); **bold** means split loses:

| heads, layout | 1 tok | 8 tok | 16 tok | 32 tok | 64 tok | 128 tok |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8, 512+0 | 8.4 / 101.8 | 12.9 / 98.6 | 19.3 / 104.0 | 31.0 / 98.4 | 53.7 / 98.3 | **101.7 / 99.0** |
| 16, 512+64 | 10.1 / 143.9 | 15.9 / 140.8 | 24.4 / 134.4 | 40.1 / 129.8 | 73.6 / 126.0 | **143.2 / 125.1** |
| 32, 512+64 | 13.6 / 149.9 | 26.5 / 144.3 | 45.8 / 138.0 | 85.9 / 133.1 | **173.7 / 130.5** | **337.5 / 130.0** |
| 64, 512+0 | 17.9 / 122.1 | 39.4 / 117.8 | 73.7 / 123.4 | **147.1 / 116.7** | **284.7 / 116.2** | **571.5 / 119.6** |
| 64, 512+64 | 18.0 / 186.7 | 39.1 / 181.7 | 72.7 / 177.0 | 144.5 / 171.1 | **279.6 / 167.7** | **536.1 / 170.9** |
| 128, 512+64 | 18.4 / 181.3 | 72.2 / 179.2 | 147.7 / 173.8 | **293.0 / 167.8** | **571.1 / 170.1** | n/a |

Split wins at <= 1024 tokens x padded heads for every shape and first loses between 1536 and 2048, so the budget is 1024.

## Accuracy Tests

**GSM8K: 97.27%**

`sgl-eval run gsm8k` (48 threads, max tokens 16384, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95). Server as in the speed tests, without `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*` and with `--reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

H200 x8, `--tp-size 8 --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`, EAGLE 5/1/6, `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=5 SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token`. Random 8192 in / 1024 out, `--num-prompts 16*C --warmup-requests 4*C`.

| C | main (tok/s/user) | this PR (tok/s/user) | change | TPOT main -> PR (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 371.4 | 412.5 | +11.1% | 2.41 -> 2.15 |
| 4 | 192.6 | 201.3 | +4.5% | 4.31 -> 4.08 |
| 8 | 139.6 | 142.7 | +2.2% | 5.80 -> 5.64 |
| 16 | 102.6 | 103.1 | +0.6% | 7.38 -> 7.32 |

From C=11, verify (C x 6 tokens) is past the cutoff and keeps the single-pass kernel; only the draft steps change. TTFT is unchanged.

+_is_sm90 = is_sm90_supported()

@@ -1357,6 +1363,19 @@ def main(
     return main
 
 
+# Measured on H200 over 8-128 heads, cold L2: split wins at <= 1024 on every shape;
+# it first loses at 1536-2048. Re-tune when either kernel changes.
+_CUDA_BF16_SPLIT_MAX_TOKEN_HEADS = 1024
+
+
+def _use_cuda_bf16_split(*, num_tokens: int, num_heads: int) -> bool:
+    # Only swept on SM90; Blackwell keeps the single-pass kernel until measured.
+    if num_heads % 4 != 0 or not _is_sm90:
+        return False
+    padded_heads = max(1 << (num_heads - 1).bit_length(), 16)
+    return num_tokens * padded_heads <= _CUDA_BF16_SPLIT_MAX_TOKEN_HEADS
+
+
 def tilelang_sparse_fwd(
     q: torch.Tensor,
     kv: torch.Tensor,
@@ -1372,13 +1391,16 @@ def tilelang_sparse_fwd(
     assert topk % 64 == 0, "topk must be padded to a multiple of 64"
 
     is_fp8_kv = kv.dtype in (torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.float8_e4m3fnuz)
-    if _is_hip or is_fp8_kv:
+    use_cuda_bf16_split = not (_is_hip or is_fp8_kv) and _use_cuda_bf16_split(

+    )
+    if _is_hip or is_fp8_kv or use_cuda_bf16_split:
         if is_fp8_kv:
             if q.dtype != kv.dtype:
                 q = q.to(kv.dtype)
             if not _is_hip:
                 block_I, threads, block_per_cu = 32, 128, 1
-                cu = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(q.device).multi_processor_count
+                cu = get_device_core_count(q.device.index)
             elif _is_gfx95_supported:
                 block_I, threads, block_per_cu, cu = 64, 256, 2, 256
             else:
@@ -1396,12 +1418,18 @@ def tilelang_sparse_fwd(
                 threads=threads,
             )
         else:
-            if _is_gfx95_supported:
-                block_I, threads, block_per_cu, cu = 64, 256, 2, 256
+            if use_cuda_bf16_split:
+                # One KV tile per CTA: the batch is too small to fill the GPU.
+                block_I, threads = 64, 256
+                ni = topk // block_I
+                inner_iter = 1
             else:
-                block_I, threads, block_per_cu, cu = 32, 128, 1, 304
-            ni = topk // block_I
-            inner_iter = _pick_inner_iter(q.shape[0], ni, cu, block_per_cu)
+                if _is_gfx95_supported:

             kernel_partial = sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial(
                 num_heads,
                 d_v,

@@ -2,6 +2,7 @@
 
 import math
 import unittest
+from unittest import mock
 
 import torch
 
@@ -11,7 +12,7 @@
     dequantize_k_cache_paged,
 )
 from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa.quant_k_cache import quantize_k_cache
-from sglang.srt.utils import is_gfx95_supported, is_hip
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_gfx95_supported, is_hip, is_sm90_supported
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci, register_cuda_ci
 from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
 
@@ -96,6 +97,14 @@ def _assert_matches_torch(self, use_fp8, d_v, d_tail):
             kv = kv.to(FP8_DTYPE)
         reference_q = q.to(FP8_DTYPE) if use_fp8 else q
 
+        if not is_hip() and not use_fp8:
+            from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa.tilelang_kernel import (
+                _use_cuda_bf16_split,
+            )
+
+            # These cases cover the single-pass v1/v2 kernels; the split path has its own test.
+            self.assertFalse(_use_cuda_bf16_split(num_tokens=tokens, num_heads=heads))
+
         scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(dim)
         expected = _torch_sparse_attention(reference_q, kv, indices, scale, d_v)
         # the partial/combine path returns [batch=1, tokens, heads, d_v]
@@ -128,6 +137,69 @@ def test_tail64_layout_unchanged_by_zero_tail_specialization(self):
             with self.subTest(use_fp8=use_fp8):
                 self._assert_matches_torch(use_fp8=use_fp8, d_v=512, d_tail=64)
 
+    @unittest.skipUnless(is_sm90_supported(), "CUDA BF16 split dispatch is SM90-only")
+    def test_cuda_bf16_split_gate_scales_with_heads(self):
+        """Split cost grows with tokens * padded heads, so 64/128-head ranks must stop splitting at 16/8 tokens, not 64."""
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa.tilelang_kernel import (
+            _use_cuda_bf16_split,
+        )
+
+        for heads, last_split_tokens in ((64, 16), (128, 8)):
+            with self.subTest(heads=heads):
+                for tokens, expected in (
+                    (last_split_tokens, True),
+                    (last_split_tokens + 1, False),
+                ):
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        _use_cuda_bf16_split(num_tokens=tokens, num_heads=heads),
+                        expected,
+                        f"{tokens=}",
+                    )
+        # The combine kernel reduces 4 heads per block.
+        self.assertFalse(_use_cuda_bf16_split(num_tokens=1, num_heads=6))
+
+    @unittest.skipUnless(is_sm90_supported(), "CUDA BF16 split dispatch is SM90-only")
+    def test_cuda_bf16_small_batch_split_matches_torch_and_graph(self):
+        """Both sides of the 8-head cutoff must take the expected kernel and match torch, eager and under graph replay."""
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa import tilelang_kernel
+
+        # GLM-5.3-Flash at TP8: 8 heads (padded to 16 in-kernel), 512+0 latent,
+        # k-pool topk 2048 + tail padded to 2112 with masked columns.
+        heads, d_v, topk, kv_len = 8, 512, 2112, 4096
+        torch.manual_seed(7)
+        kv = torch.randn(kv_len, 1, d_v, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(d_v)
+        for tokens, expect_split in ((64, True), (65, False)):
+            with self.subTest(tokens=tokens):
+                q = torch.randn(tokens, heads, d_v, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+                indices = torch.randint(
+                    0, kv_len, (tokens, 1, topk), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+                )
+                indices[..., 2051:] = -1
+                indices[0, :, 1:] = -1  # a row with one live column
+                expected = _torch_sparse_attention(q, kv, indices, scale, d_v)
+                with mock.patch.object(
+                    tilelang_kernel,
+                    "sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial",
+                    wraps=tilelang_kernel.sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial,
+                ) as partial_factory:
+                    actual = tilelang_kernel.tilelang_sparse_fwd(
+                        q, kv, indices, scale, d_v=d_v
+                    )
+                self.assertEqual(partial_factory.called, expect_split)
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    actual.squeeze(0), expected, atol=0.04, rtol=0.04
+                )
+
+                graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+                with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+                    captured = tilelang_kernel.tilelang_sparse_fwd(
+                        q, kv, indices, scale, d_v=d_v
+                    )
+                graph.replay()
+                torch.cuda.synchronize()
+                torch.testing.assert_close(captured, actual, atol=0, rtol=0)
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
